title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 38 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record provides updates on current public health signals and respiratory virus activity and presents detailed epidemiological analyses of cholera, epidemic meningitis and human plague. During epidemiological week 38, WHO screened more than 582 000 signals for potential public health threats, while global surveillance showed low influenza and respiratory syncytial virus activity and stable, low SARS-CoV-2 positivity.

The issue reports 451 499 cholera cases and 7870 deaths from 47 countries in 2025; although reported cases declined compared with 2024, deaths increased and the burden remained concentrated in several heavily affected countries. It also reviews meningitis surveillance and control in the African meningitis belt, including epidemic activity, laboratory surveillance and vaccination, and examines human plague reported during 2019–2025, highlighting its continued geographical concentration. Together, these reports emphasize the importance of sustained epidemiological and laboratory surveillance, timely and complete reporting, vaccination and preparedness for detecting and responding to epidemic-prone diseases.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 36-37 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record reports on selected global public health events and disease surveillance developments in September 2026. It summarizes signals and events identified through WHO public health intelligence activities during epidemiological weeks 36 and 37 and provides an update on global respiratory virus activity, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus. It also presents an assessment of influenza at the human-animal interface, covering newly reported human infections with influenza viruses of animal origin, their circulation in animals and associated public health risk.

The issue includes the global leprosy (Hansen disease) update for 2025, reviewing progress at the midpoint of the Global Leprosy Strategy 2021–2030. It presents global and regional trends in new case detection, childhood cases and grade-2 disability, and emphasizes early detection, person-centred care, contact screening and post-exposure prophylaxis, antimicrobial resistance surveillance and meaningful participation of people affected by leprosy as integral to achieving and sustaining elimination.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 35 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record provides updates on public health signals and events, global respiratory virus activity and the multi-country cholera outbreak. During epidemiological week 35 (24–30 August 2026), WHO screened 621 233 signals through digital event-based surveillance, assessed 35 signals or events and escalated 23 for operational attention. Global surveillance for week 34 indicated that influenza and SARS-CoV-2 positivity remained stable and low overall, while respiratory syncytial virus positivity also remained low globally.

The cholera update reports 57 652 new cholera and acute watery diarrhoea cases and 471 associated deaths from 19 countries across four WHO regions in July 2026. From 1 January to 26 July, 221 365 cases and 2153 deaths were reported from 28 countries, with the African Region recording the highest numbers of cases and deaths. The report highlights substantial variation in transmission between countries and cautions that underreporting, reporting delays and differences in surveillance and laboratory capacity affect data comparability.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 34 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record presents updates on public health intelligence, global respiratory virus activity and vaccine and medicine safety. During epidemiological week 34 (17–23 August 2026), WHO public health intelligence teams screened approximately 604 275 signals through digital event-based surveillance, with 31 signals or events assessed and 21 escalated for operational attention. Global respiratory virus surveillance for week 33 indicated influenza positivity below 10% and low SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus activity globally.

The issue also summarizes the fifth joint meeting of the Advisory Committee on Safety of Medicinal Products and the Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety, held in June 2026. Discussions addressed smart pharmacovigilance, risk communication, maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination, adverse events of special interest, Ebola, and safety monitoring of mpox, human papillomavirus and acellular pertussis vaccines, emphasizing continued pharmacovigilance, strengthened surveillance systems and collection of safety data, particularly in low- and middle-income countries and vulnerable populations.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 33 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record presents WHO Public Health Intelligence activities for epidemiological week 33 (10–16 August 2026) and examines the ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the context of the two previously documented BVD outbreaks, in Uganda in 2007–2008 and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2012. During the reporting week, digital event-based surveillance screened approximately 627 661 raw signals, of which 20 underwent further assessment and 14 were escalated for operational attention.

Comparison of the three BVD outbreaks shows that laboratory confirmation has become progressively faster, while delays in recognizing and escalating early evidence of transmission remain a recurring challenge. The 2026 outbreak is occurring across highly connected populations amid insecurity, displacement and a humanitarian emergency, increasing the consequences of delayed detection. The analysis emphasizes rapid investigation of unexplained deaths and illness among health-care workers and broader ebolavirus testing when initial species-specific testing is negative.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 32 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record contains two main components. The first, “Highlighted Signals and Events”, summarizes WHO Public Health Intelligence activities during epidemiological week 32 (3–9 August 2026), including digital event-based surveillance for the early detection and assessment of potential public health threats, newly verified events and published rapid risk assessments.

The issue also presents the 2026 WHO position paper on typhoid vaccines, which updates and replaces the 2018 position paper and focuses primarily on typhoid conjugate vaccines (TCVs). It recommends TCVs for routine immunization in typhoid-endemic countries, particularly where typhoid incidence, case fatality or antimicrobial resistance is high, with catch-up vaccination at introduction. Recommendations also address booster doses, vaccination during outbreaks and use in fragile, conflict-affected and vulnerable settings. The paper identifies remaining evidence gaps concerning duration of protection, booster schedules and TCV use in outbreak response.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 31 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record provides an update on WHO public health intelligence activities and selected public health events reported during epidemiological week 31 (27 July–2 August 2026). Through digital event-based surveillance, WHO Public Health Intelligence teams screened and assessed signals from multiple sources to support early detection and evaluation of potential health threats. The report summarizes signal assessment metrics, newly identified events and published information products, including a Disease Outbreak News item.

The issue also presents a global epidemiological update on the multi-country cholera outbreak, including reported cases and deaths from January to June 2026, regional trends and detailed overviews of affected countries. It highlights factors contributing to transmission, including conflict, population displacement, inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene conditions, and challenges affecting surveillance and response. The report provides data visualizations, regional analyses and technical resources to support interpretation and ongoing cholera preparedness and response activities.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 30 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record brings together updates on global public health surveillance and immunization policy. It includes the weekly Highlighted Signals and Events summary, reporting the outcomes of WHO Public Health Intelligence digital event-based surveillance during epidemiological week 30 (20–26 July 2026), including selected signals, surveillance metrics, and information products that support the early detection and assessment of potential public health threats. The issue also features a preliminary analysis of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, examining surveillance alerts, alert system performance, and operational challenges associated with outbreak detection and response.

The main feature is the WHO Position Paper on COVID-19 vaccines – July 2026, which presents updated WHO recommendations on the use of COVID-19 vaccines in the context of sustained SARS-CoV-2 circulation following the end of the Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in 2023, widespread population immunity, and the availability of Omicron-adapted vaccines. Developed on the basis of recommendations from the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) on Immunization, the paper reviews the latest evidence on COVID-19 epidemiology, populations at increased risk of hospitalization and death, and the effectiveness, impact, safety, and cost-effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines. It provides WHO policy recommendations for routine COVID-19 vaccination, with particular emphasis on populations at highest risk of severe outcomes, offers guidance on vaccine product selection, vaccination schedules, and coadministration, and identifies key evidence gaps and priorities for future research.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 29 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly epidemiological record presents three public health updates. It summarizes WHO Public Health Intelligence activities conducted during epidemiological week 29 (13–19 July 2026), highlighting digital event-based surveillance outputs, selected signals and events requiring operational attention, and the publication of a Disease Outbreak News report. It also provides a global dengue update based on surveillance data through the end of June 2026, describing recent epidemiological trends, regional and country-level distribution of reported cases and deaths, surveillance considerations, and WHO’s support for prevention and control through the Global Arbovirus Initiative, including vector control, surveillance, preparedness, community engagement, and climate-informed response.

The issue also summarizes the 41st Meeting of the International Task Force for Disease Eradication on the elimination of trachoma as a public health problem. It reviews global progress towards the 2030 elimination target, implementation of the SAFE strategy, validation experiences, persistent operational and epidemiological challenges, and emerging evidence to strengthen programme implementation. The report discusses approaches to addressing persistent and recrudescent trachoma, interventions in insecure settings, advances in surveillance and diagnostics, and priorities for sustaining elimination efforts through evidence-based, multisectoral action.

title: Weekly Epidemiological Record, 2026, vol. 101, 28 [full issue]
description:
This issue of the Weekly Epidemiological Record presents three public health updates. It summarizes WHO Public Health Intelligence activities during epidemiological week 28 (6–12 July 2026), reporting the results of global digital event-based surveillance, including the assessment and escalation of signals of potential public health importance and recently verified events. It also provides a global epidemiological update on SARS-CoV-2, reviewing recent trends in virus circulation, reported cases, deaths, test positivity, regional patterns, variant distribution, wastewater surveillance and the current limitations affecting surveillance data and interpretation.

The issue further reports on progress towards the global elimination of trachoma during 2025–2026. It reviews the epidemiology of trachoma, implementation of the SAFE strategy, country validation status, populations requiring interventions and updated estimates of the global burden of disease based on evaluation-unit data reported to WHO. The report summarizes progress achieved through surgery, antibiotic distribution, facial cleanliness and environmental improvement, highlighting continuing reductions in populations requiring interventions while identifying countries where elimination activities and surveillance remain necessary.
